newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN says Saybolt's inspection in Iraq last step.
newsitem.headline: UN says Saybolt's inspection in Iraq last step.

text.p: The United Nations said on Monday that an inspection of oil metering equipment by the Dutch firm Saybolt was the last step before Iraq's oil-for-food program could start running.
But spokeswoman Sylvana Foa did not give a start date for the plan which U.N. officials hope could begin next week.
She said Saybolt was supposed to get to Iraq on Tuesday and it would take them a "couple of days to ascertain that this meter is now working."

"And that is the last pending item on our list," before a report from Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali to the Security Council that would automatically trigger the program. Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months in order to purchase badly-needed food, medicine and other necessities.
The report should be no more than one page long, she said after which "it is all systems go."
Saybolt, retained by the United Nations, is to ensure faulty equipment at the Zakho station along the Iraq-Turkey border is operational.
